records.citation: OpenStax. Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 11.5: Muscles of the Pectoral Girdle and Upper Limbs. 2022.
records.population: Foundational human anatomy reference; not a training intervention population.
records.limitations: An anatomy textbook supports names and broad actions, not exercise efficacy, individual technique, regional hypertrophy or prescription dose.

records.citation: OpenStax. Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 11.6: Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs. 2022.
records.population: Foundational human anatomy reference; not a training intervention population.
records.limitations: An anatomy textbook supports names and broad actions, not exercise efficacy, individual technique, regional hypertrophy or prescription dose.

records.citation: Kassiano W, et al. Does Varying Resistance Exercises Promote Superior Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains? A Systematic Review. J Strength Cond Res. 2022;36(6):1753-1762.
records.population: Young men in eight resistance-training studies (total n=241).
records.limitations: Only eight studies and all participants were young men. It does not validate a universal exercise rotation or a SportRX muscle-coverage score.

records.citation: Haugen ME, et al. Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance: a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil. 2023;15(1):103.
records.population: Adults aged 18-60 years in 13 comparative studies; hypertrophy was reported in five studies.
records.limitations: Hypertrophy evidence came from five studies. Similar group-level hypertrophy does not make exercises mechanically identical or equally suitable for every person.

records.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J. Effects of range of motion on muscle development during resistance training interventions: A systematic review. SAGE Open Med. 2020;8:2050312120901559.
records.population: Healthy adults in longitudinal resistance-training range-of-motion studies.
records.limitations: The evidence favored full range for lower-limb hypertrophy, while upper-body evidence was limited and conflicting. It does not define a safe individual range.

records.citation: Varovic D, et al. Does Muscle Length Influence Regional Hypertrophy? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Int J Sports Med. 2025;46(14):1027-1036.
records.population: Young adults in 12 resistance-training studies that measured regional hypertrophy.
records.limitations: Estimated effects were small or trivial with uncertainty and were drawn from young adults. The review does not support deterministic exercise rankings.

records.citation: Nunes JP, et al. What influence does resistance exercise order have on muscular strength gains and muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Sport Sci. 2021;21(2):149-157.
records.population: Healthy adults in resistance-training exercise-order studies.
records.limitations: Hypertrophy evidence was limited and did not show a clear order effect. Priority-first language applies more directly to exercise-specific strength outcomes.

records.citation: Gentil P, et al. A Review of the Acute Effects and Long-Term Adaptations of Single- and Multi-Joint Exercises during Resistance Training. Sports Med. 2017;47(5):843-855.
records.population: Healthy participants in studies comparing single-joint, multi-joint, or combined resistance exercise approaches.
records.limitations: The comparative literature was small and concentrated in upper-limb outcomes. It does not prove that isolation work is always unnecessary or always required.
